beats.label: Prove the HMAC math offline
beats.cue: “HMAC-SHA256 over v0:timestamp:body, compared constant-time. Sign a body with a demo secret: it verifies. Append one space: it doesn't. No Slack workspace involved.”
beats.script: HMAC-SHA256 over v0:timestamp:body, compared constant-time. Sign a body with a demo secret: it verifies. Append one space: it doesn't. No Slack workspace involved. [[pause:1.5s]] No credentials are involved in this check; a clean exit confirms the local path behaves as described. Prints `true` then `false` using the adapter the bundle installed (verifySlackSignature + signSlackBody from @crewhaus/channel-adapter-slack); the ±5 min replay window and the timingSafeEqual compare are in that same file.
beats.command: bun -e 'const v = await import("./live/dist/node_modules/@crewhaus/channel-adapter-slack/dist/verify.js"); const body = "{}", ts = Math.floor(Date.now() / 1000), secret = "demo-signing-secret"; const headers = new Headers({ "x-slack-request-timestamp": String(ts), "x-slack-signature": v.signSlackBody({ body, timestamp: ts, signingSecret: secret }) }); console.log("as Slack signed it:", v.verifySlackSignature({ headers, body, signingSecret: secret })); console.log("one byte appended:", v.verifySlackSignature({ headers, body: body + " ", signingSecret: secret }));'

verify.note: prints `true` then `false` using the adapter the bundle installed (verifySlackSignature + signSlackBody from @crewhaus/channel-adapter-slack); the ±5 min replay window and the timingSafeEqual compare are in that same file

beats.cue: “And that signature says nothing about what's inside the body. So the codegen already classifies every inbound at TrustOrigin channel before it seeds a model turn — this is the line, in the file it ships in.”
beats.script: And that signature says nothing about what's inside the body. So the codegen already classifies every inbound at TrustOrigin channel before it seeds a model turn — this is the line, in the file it ships in. Imports classifyInbound from @crewhaus/channel-adapter-base and calls it on args.message before runChatLoop — which is exactly why Step 6 tells you NOT to add a pre-model hook that classifies the same text again.

beats.label: Boot the daemon with no secrets
beats.cue: “Strip the four env vars back out and it names every one it needs before it opens a socket — exit 2. That's the $VAR_NAME lowering doing its job.”
beats.script: Strip the four env vars back out and it names every one it needs before it opens a socket — exit 2. That's the $VAR_NAME lowering doing its job. [[pause:1.5s]] The refusal is the proof in this beat, so the verifier expects exit code 2. Designed refusal `[daemon] missing required env vars: SLACK_BOT_TOKEN, SLACK_SIGNING_SECRET, ANTHROPIC_AUTH_TOKEN or ANTHROPIC_API_KEY`.
beats.command: env -u SLACK_BOT_TOKEN -u SLACK_SIGNING_SECRET -u ANTHROPIC_AUTH_TOKEN -u ANTHROPIC_API_KEY bun live/dist/daemon.ts

verify.note: designed refusal — `[daemon] missing required env vars: SLACK_BOT_TOKEN, SLACK_SIGNING_SECRET, ANTHROPIC_AUTH_TOKEN or ANTHROPIC_API_KEY`. `env -u` makes it deterministic: Setup already sourced .env into this same terminal, and with the four present the daemon would boot and listen instead

beats.label: Pre-flight the env the daemon boots on
beats.cue: “Before you own a Slack app at all: which env vars does this daemon need? Scrub them and the scope doctor lists all three and exits 1 — deterministic enough for CI.”
beats.script: Before you own a Slack app at all: which env vars does this daemon need? Scrub them and the scope doctor lists all three and exits 1 — deterministic enough for CI. [[pause:1.5s]] The nonzero result is intentional: this command expects exit code 1. `--offline` is the env checks only, no network: 3 checks, 3 failed → exit 1. With .env sourced (as it is on camera) the same command exits 0, so the beat scrubs the vars to stay deterministic.
beats.command: env -u SLACK_BOT_TOKEN -u SLACK_SIGNING_SECRET -u ANTHROPIC_AUTH_TOKEN -u ANTHROPIC_API_KEY crewhaus channel verify live/crewhaus.yaml --offline

verify.note: `--offline` is the env checks only, no network: 3 checks, 3 failed → exit 1. With .env sourced (as it is on camera) the same command exits 0, so the beat scrubs the vars to stay deterministic. Drop `--offline` and it becomes the live auth.test + granted-scopes doctor, which needs the token
